subject: POC: Success criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: POC: Success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Recap and proposed next steps below so we have alignment before scheduling the trial kickoff.

Quick recap
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for Atlas Payments use cases (payment intent classification + automated reconciliation assistant).
- Trial length proposed: 2 weeks (we can extend if needed).

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (please review and flag changes)
- Latency: P95 generation latency < 350 ms for representative prompts (measured with 99th percentile excluded warm-up).
- Throughput: sustained 300 req/s for peak batch (target steady-state), with ability to burst to 500 req/s for short windows.
- Cost: average cost per token <= $0.0006 (including any batching/quantization adjustments).
- Quality: intent accuracy (top-1) >= 92% on your labeled set; hallucination/incorrect info rate < 1%; answer freshness and regulatory redaction checks pass.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability for the trial window.

Evaluation plan (high level)
- Week 0: onboarding & instrumentation — Redwood provides test harness and traffic generator; Atlas provides sample traffic & labeled set.
- Week 1: baseline run against Atlas traffic — collect latency, throughput, cost, and quality metrics.
- Week 2: optimizations & tuning (batching, quant profiles, model variant) — measure deltas and produce final report.

Ownership
- Atlas: provide representative traffic (anonymized), success-labeled examples, and security contacts.
- Redwood: provide test harness, dashboards, measurement scripts, and optimization recommendations.

Attachments: POC-success-criteria-v1.xlsx, POC-eval-plan.docx (high-level matrix + timeline).

Ask / next steps
1) Confirm the success criteria above (especially throughput/cost targets) or propose edits by EOD tomorrow.
2) Once agreed, we’ll schedule a 60-min kickoff (preferably Mon morning) and share the onboarding checklist.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@atlaspay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@atlaspay.com
Date: 2027-10-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Thanks Jordan — great recap. A few small edits/questions from our end:

- Throughput: can we set the steady-state target to 300 req/s (sustained) rather than 500? We do want the ability to burst higher, but 300 steady is our more realistic expectation.
- Cost: $0.0006/token looks reasonable as a target but can you include expected ranges for quantized runs (8-bit) vs unquantized in the eval report?
- Security: our security team will send an initial questionnaire (SOC2 scope and data handling) — please route answers to security@atlaspay.com.
- SLA: can Redwood confirm expected availability target for the trial (we typically require 99.9%).

Also, could you share the traffic generator scripts and the baseline harness so we can validate locally before the kickoff?

On timing: Monday morning for a kickoff works for our PM — happy to block a 60-min slot once we lock criteria.

Alex Turner
Director, Platform Engineering | Atlas Payments
alex.turner@atlaspay.com

> Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Recap and proposed next steps below so we have alignment before scheduling the trial kickoff.
> ...
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Alex — appreciate the quick reply and good points. Agreed to update the targets as you suggested. Summary of changes and concrete commitments below: 

Updated targets
- Latency: P95 < 350 ms (no change).
- Throughput: steady-state 300 req/s; staged ramp to 300 over first 5 business days; burst capacity up to 500 req/s for short windows.
- Cost: include quantization delta estimates in the v2 eval sheet (attached).
- Reliability: Redwood will target 99.9% availability during the trial window; we’ll document fallbacks and escalation path.

Commitments
- Redwood to provide:
  • Traffic generator + baseline harness (Python scripts + container).
  • A pre-configured Grafana dashboard and CSV export of metrics.
  • A short onboarding runbook and SRE contact list.
- Atlas to provide:
  • Representative traffic (anonymized) and labeled examples for quality checks.
  • Security questionnaire responses and point-of-contact.

I’ve attached POC-plan-v2.xlsx with the metrics matrix and a tentative timeline. Drive link to shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-Eval-Metrics

Next steps
1) Alex / security: expect the security questionnaire from your team — we’ll respond within 48 hours.
2) Atlas: share anonymized sample traffic by EOD Friday (the sooner we have it, the faster we can run baseline).
3) Jordan/Marissa: we’ll provision the trial environment and share the traffic generator repo.
4) Schedule a 60-minute kickoff for Monday morning — I’ll propose 9:00 AM PT and send a calendar invite.

Attachments: POC-plan-v2.xlsx

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

- SRE/capacity planning + trial infra: Lauren Bishop (please confirm GPUs and scaling policy we intend to use for this POC).

Immediate actions

- Lauren: please confirm the instance specs and a proposed autoscale ramp (we should support staged ramp to 300 req/s in 5 days).
- Jordan: send the calendar invite for Monday 09:00 AM PT and attach onboarding checklist.

Also: prepare a short note for the security answers (SOC2 scope) — I’ll coordinate with security to ensure we answer within 48 hours.

Marissa
